sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

content.text:
Case F21: segment the fibrous soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 267x267x505 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case F21 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(267, 267, 505) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: fibrous soft-tissue tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 252/505 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm noticing a large heterogeneous mass in the posterior compartment of the thigh on the sagittal image, so I want to check the axial sequence for more detail.

content.text: sheet axial 60–460/505 (12 slices) | v0 | tool calls 2/40, prompts 0/15
sheet sagittal 60–220/267 (8 slices) | v0 | tool calls 3/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm trying to orient myself with the sagittal and axial views—the mass appears bright in the posterior thigh around axial slices 270-370, sitting in the superior portion of the sagittal image. I want to check axial slice 315 to get a clearer look.

content.text: axial 315/505 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 4/40, prompts 0/15
Mass is clear. Use multiple positive points.

version v1 (parent v0) | volume 855.1 mL | components 14 (largest 99.9%; 13 others total 0.5 mL) | extent axial 127–384, coronal 23–143, sagittal 86–211 | change +855.1 mL / 0.0 mL | tool calls 5/40, prompts 1/15 | point add (6 mark(s)) | image: axial 294, coronal 81, sagittal 143 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: This 855 mL mass is large, extending down to axial 127. I'm checking the inferior tail and noticing a posterior compartment region at axial 242 with striated, bright signal tissue - this could represent edema or muscle infiltration, or possibly tumor extension like a desmoid process. I'm cross-referencing the coronal images to confirm the tail's extent.

content.text: axial 230/505 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 7/40, prompts 1/15
coronal 95/267 | crop full | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 6/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: This coronal volume looks reformatted since axial slice thickness is greater. At axial 230, the mask picks up striated muscle with feathery edema patterns rather than tumor, while the actual tumor is a well-defined bright mass spanning axial 278-370. I'll check axial 270 to find the lower boundary of the mass.

content.text: sheet axial 240–300/505 (8 slices) | v1 | tool calls 8/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
The striated pattern around 240-266 looks like normal muscle fascicles, possibly consistent with a desmoid's fascial tail tapering into the mass around slice 270-274. I'll mark the boundary around 266-268 as the transition from muscle to tumor.

I'll erase slices 127-268, using a large polygon eraser on the axial view with coarse marks placed well outside the region of interest.

content.text: axial 268/505 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 9/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: The lower pole of the tumor is ill-defined, and desmoids can infiltrate muscle, so the striated pattern around 240-257 likely reflects muscle edema rather than tumor. I'll limit the annotation to the clearly defined mass, erasing up to slice 262 and keeping the transition zone at 263 onward.

content.text: version v2 (parent v1) | volume 665.0 mL | components 4 (largest 99.9%; 3 others total 0.0 mL) | extent axial 263–384, coronal 23–143, sagittal 86–211 | change +0.0 mL / -190.1 mL | tool calls 10/40, prompts 1/15 | paint erase on 163 slice(s) | image: axial 315, coronal 78, sagittal 145 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: The bottom edge looks flat-cut in this view, but the coronal slice suggests the mass might extend a bit lower centrally — I should try the refine step and see if that reshapes the boundary without reintroducing the tail artifact.

content.text: version v3 (parent v2) | volume 737.8 mL | components 19 (largest 99.9%; 18 others total 0.9 mL) | extent axial 145–382, coronal 23–140, sagittal 86–211 | change +93.9 mL / -21.1 mL | tool calls 11/40, prompts 2/15 | refine from current mask | image: axial 307, coronal 79, sagittal 145 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: The lower pole looks rounded and plausible, but the extent stretches to 145 because of small extra components. I should keep only the largest component, and I need a mark inside it to do that correctly—I recall mark 1374 being inside at axial 315, so I'll switch to that view and use it to keep the right component.

content.text: axial 315/505 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v3 | tool calls 12/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking: I'm looking at the left edge of the outline, which includes a darker rim band between the bright mass and outer fascia—likely compressed muscle tissue like the biceps femoris. This component seems fine to keep as part of the boundary.

content.text: version v4 (parent v3) | volume 736.8 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 200–382, coronal 23–140, sagittal 86–211 | change +0.0 mL / -0.9 mL | tool calls 13/40, prompts 2/15 | edit keep_component | image: axial 307, coronal 79, sagittal 145 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: I'm still seeing extent at axial 200, with what looks like a thin tail extending further down, and the coronal view also shows a tail toward the bottom—so I should check slice 240 to confirm.

content.text: sheet axial 200–270/505 (8 slices) | v4 | tool calls 14/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking:
I keep noticing the grey, striated region around 250-260 that stands out from the darker surrounding muscle — it could be tumor infiltrating the posterior compartment muscle, or possibly just edematous muscle from compression rather than true tumor involvement.

Given the ambiguity, I decide to erase the signal between slices 195-238, since the coronal view shows the mass's lower pole tapering smoothly through that range, while keeping the bright region at 240+ that resembles the mass's own signal characteristics.

content.text: axial 238/505 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay outline | v4 | tool calls 15/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking: Checking the slice range around 238 and nearby levels, it looks like striated muscle with edema rather than the masked structure I was looking for, remaining striated through 250-268 with a smooth central area only appearing later. I'll adjust the erase range to roughly 190-255.

content.text: version v5 (parent v4) | volume 676.8 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 256–382, coronal 23–140, sagittal 86–211 | change +0.0 mL / -60.0 mL | tool calls 16/40, prompts 2/15 | paint erase on 66 slice(s) | image: axial 313, coronal 78, sagittal 146 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: Looking at the coronal and sagittal views, the removed region appears to blend into the mass as a greyish continuation, though the reformats are blurry compared to the axial, making it hard to be certain whether that lower tail truly extends the lesion or is an artifact of poor resolution.

content.text: sheet axial 340–395/505 (8 slices) | v5 | tool calls 17/40, prompts 2/15

content.thinking: The superior end looks good. I'm checking the middle slice boundary now, since around 315 the left side included that darker rim edge, and doing a final pass over everything.

arguments.reason: Main mass well captured; inferior extent into edematous striated muscle ambiguous.

content.text:
Final review of v5: volume 676.8 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 256–382, coronal 23–140, sagittal 86–211 | tool calls 18/40, prompts 2/15. The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. Candidates (second image): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong).
C1 add 838 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly anterior of the mask
C2 add 704 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly anterior of the mask
C3 add 514 mL, touches mask on its left, right and posterior sides, level with the mask
C4 add 2.8 mL, does not touch the mask, mostly inferior of the mask
candidate image: one row per candidate, columns axial / coronal / sagittal through the candidate (green outline = current mask, magenta outline + light tint = candidate; judge the tissue inside the magenta outline). For each candidate decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept) or normal tissue (reject). Accept with seg_accept and call seg_finish again for a new review; if none belong, confirm with the review code. If everything is right, call seg_finish again with review_code "4699" to save it.

content.thinking: These candidates look like shells, so I'll reject them. The flat bottom cut at 256 shows a minor spur at the bottom-left near sag 117, but it's negligible enough to accept as is.

arguments.reason: Main mass well captured in all planes; inferior boundary vs edematous striated muscle is ambiguous.

content.text: case F21 finished (confidence medium); final mask saved from v5 | final volume 676.8 mL, components 1 (largest 100.0%) | tool calls 19/40, prompts 2/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

content.thinking: I should be honest about the shape overall, noting that the bottom edge is just a flat cut rather than a rounded or natural curve.

content.text:
I've saved the mask for the fibrous soft-tissue tumor at medium confidence: 676.8 mL, one connected piece, spanning axial slices 256–382. The main uncertainty is where the tumor's lower end really is.

- **Location:** a large mass of mixed brightness in the back of the thigh. It is clearly visible from about axial slice 270 up to about 380.
- **Main body and upper end:** the outline follows the mass edge well in all three planes. The upper end tapers out by about slice 380.
- **Lower end (uncertain):** below the mass, the model kept spreading down to slice ~127 along muscle with a streaky, feathery pattern. To me that looks like swollen (edematous) muscle rather than tumor, so I erased everything below slice 256. Fibrous tumors of this kind can grow into neighbouring muscle, though, and in the coronal and sagittal views that tissue looks like a gradual continuation of the mass. If it is tumor, the mask is too small at the bottom.
- **Cut shape:** the erase leaves a flat lower edge at slice 256 rather than a natural boundary. Slices 256–268 include some of that same streaky tissue, so the true edge could sit a few slices higher or several centimetres lower.
- **Edge band:** on the outer-back side of the mass, the outline takes in part of a darker band. It is probably compressed muscle rather than a tumor capsule.
- **Suggestions rejected:** the automatic suggestions in the final review were either rings around the whole thigh or the same streaky muscle below the cut, so I didn't add any.

I used 19 of the 40 tool calls and 2 of the 15 model prompts.
